chapter: Postwar clubs, Chile and New York
title: The Fourth Estate, then an all-star band at the Savoy in Boston
summary: After leaving Chicago clubs Freeman puts a band in the Fourth Estate and later brings an all-star band including Omer Simeon to Boston's Savoy for a month.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: You got to watch it and it was depressing being around there late all the time, sort of an after hours place in Chicago and it wasn't what I wanted and then -- I am trying to think what actually happened there. I broke up -- my first wife and I separated and I met another woman who owned a place and I put a band in her place. It was a place called the Fourth Estate, a newspaper men's hangout in Chicago, and we made a -- it was a very successful thing for awhile, but then she had a lot of debts and there were some Chinese people pressuring her to sell and she made some sort of promise to, I think maybe in writing I am not sure, to sell the place, so finally she had to and so she got some money out of it, and we went to New York.

She said, 'Let's go to New York where you can get back into the concerts and things, and we were in New York three days and I got an offer to go to Boston to Mrs. Donahue's place, the Savoy, and you know, very good money and of course, I had to take a band, I got an all-star band and incidentally, Omer Simeon was in that band.
And a guy by the name of Kirkpatrick, the pianist.
He was with Chuck Webb for awhile.

I can't remember the drummer but Lee Castaldo Catoido, who later became a bandleader and called himself Lee Castle. Well, he's still around of course, I think. It's difficult to remember the names. Oh, Big Chief Russell Moore.
Did you put this band together?
I put the band together just for that gig.
So you brought Simeon in from Chicago.
No, no, he was in New York. They all had to be in New York. We got on a train and went there, and we were there a month.
